declaredParameters.sourceClock: independent page performance.now/setTimeout; never advanced by logical frames
declaredParameters.profile: repeatable continuous drag/reversal/hold/up/recontact/cancel with fire/focus, fixed phase offset by seat
declaredParameters.scope: Two independent headed desktop Chromium processes, CPU rates [1,4], native GPU, independent relay with 39 +/- 5 ms one-way delay; independent native-ABI touch deadlines; not DOM/Launcher/phone evidence.
declaredParameters.label: mobile-rollback-relay39-b1

cpuThrottle.scope: openProbe and after-open counters precede CPU throttling; subsequent netplay setup and first game callback use the configured per-side rates.

touchInput.scope: Synthetic native ABI events on an independent Page clock; not a Launcher/iOS bridge or physical phone test

headedLaunch.scope: Window-mode environment control, not a production code change; proxy, input, audio/context, CPU setup, and native GPU arguments are unchanged.

runs.scope: Two separate desktop Chromium processes; native GPU; real WebSocket relay with synchronous client send and seeded relay-process input impairment; burst anchored to relay first input receive; independent Page-clock synthetic native ABI direct touch; conditional wire-to-render progress, not physical-phone or Launcher bridge evidence; sampled SDL output blocks, not speaker/acoustic acceptance

scopes.body: Every original sample in [first frontier >= startFrame, first frontier >= endFrame); no phase or rewound-cursor filtering. Without a terminal crossing the observed body is right-censored.
scopes.progress: Closed Hz and cumulative counter deltas use endpoint minus start, including the endpoint counters. The endpoint callback cost belongs to tail; body cost includes start. Missing native frontier uses explicitly labelled observed next high-water, never captures, and complete stays false.
scopes.gaps: Top-level gap fields retain body-only submission/RAF timestamp semantics. formalWithEndBoundary also closes through the terminal marker. Cross-boundary intervals and all sampled startup/tail costs remain separate. No sample is removed from raw results.
scopes.timing: callbackCompletionGapMs is the post-native sampledAt gap between renderer submissions, not whole observer callback return; RAF timestamps and submissions are not physical scanout.
scopes.phase: scenes is a compatibility alias of sessionPhases (SessionPhase, not internal MatchScene); no phase is excluded.
scopes.capture: captures is a once-only input-capture counter and may be ahead of simulation completion; it never chooses boundaries.
scopes.nativeWork: callbackWorkMs is the existing native game callback measurement, not total JavaScript observer time or GPU completion.

routeEvidence.scope: Selected ICE candidate types and channel state after measurement; no IP/SDP recorded. RTC is not automatically direct.

summaries.renderer: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics (0x0000A78B) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)

configuration.cadence: Absolute Page-clock grid during moving legs; contact/control/release/hold edges retain their own deadlines.

wireObservation.boundary: Serialized native local input first observed at the transport send-intent hook, before original send and configured client delay/drop.
wireObservation.timing: firstWireAtMs is this observation time. It is not successful send API completion, network delivery, or the exact native capture time.

source.clockIndependence: setTimeout absolute deadlines; never scheduled from game frame, capture, frontier or transport progress.

tape.scope: Rechecks retained unique 12B rows; duplicate packet comparisons remain probe-reported.

response.method: Conditional render-progress proxy: latest submitted movement event, first subsequent changed native movement wire, then first newly advanced frontier with renderer submission. This does not establish visible movement or per-event gameplay effect.
response.confounding: Focus can change joystick velocity; death/context changes can write neutral input; clipping, overwritten moves and target convergence can produce no visible movement. First wire observation can follow a capture delayed by backpressure: ordering it after an event does not prove capture followed that event. The submission touch state and changed-controls marker are metadata, not proof of causality. Normalized finger coordinates are not the absolute wire target.
response.denominator: All configured planned events remain in events + futureEvents. dueEvents and futureCensoredEvents are separate. Coalesced, blocked, clipped, unchanged and unsubmitted events cannot be inferred successful. Hold markers do not manufacture a wire edge.

relay.scope: Observed-anchor consistency only; assumes Date.now within +/-1 ms and fixed offset between anchors.

raf.clock: Page performance.now(); rafTimestamp is the browser supplied frame timestamp, not entry time.

rafAnomaly.scope: Poll observations of an existing game RAF chain. No new frames, timers, transport processing, trace capture, or production fallback. The 250 ms trigger is diagnostic, not a smoothness acceptance threshold.

clocks.pollGaps: Gaps between observations are not proof that RAF or JavaScript was blocked; only an identified request supplies wait evidence.

injection.packetScope: E9NP version 4 kind 1; ACK-only and redundant input included; non-input control/hash/signaling untouched; relay has no separate RTC repair lane.
injection.jitterAlgorithm: Per-sender LCG 1664525*x+1013904223, seed 0x915ab+sender; same formula as legacy client impairment. Relay forwarding order can differ.
injection.burstClock: First non-empty E9NP input receive in this relay process; distinct from browser active time.

rafAnomalyNodePolls.scope: Existing 100 ms status-poll CDP request/return brackets. Page clocks are separate; a missing poll is not proof of a pending RAF.

host.scope: Host-wide counters, not per-call CPU attribution. Process deltas require adjacent same pid/name.
limitations: Aggregate CPU occupancy does not establish single-core availability, CPU frequency, thermal state, GPU load, or a stable benchmark environment.
Process names are candidates for contention, not proof that a process is compiling. Known harness/relay/helper PIDs are labeled separately; other node processes remain unlabeled candidates.
Process CPU is cumulative lifetime CPU seconds. A first sighting is not CPU consumed during this run; PID reuse or counter reset can break a delta.
The 5 s process snapshots miss short tasks that start and exit between snapshots. Timer delays and source/receive times are retained.
This observer has overhead. Its own PowerShell helper is intentionally not a candidate process, but its work is included in aggregate CPU counters.
Overflow and sampling failures make this evidence incomplete; they are never a reason to silently remove a game result.

response.method: Conditional render-progress proxy: latest submitted movement event, first subsequent changed native movement wire, then first newly advanced frontier with renderer submission. This does not establish visible movement or per-event gameplay effect.
response.confounding: Focus can change joystick velocity; death/context changes can write neutral input; clipping, overwritten moves and target convergence can produce no visible movement. First wire observation can follow a capture delayed by backpressure: ordering it after an event does not prove capture followed that event. The submission touch state and changed-controls marker are metadata, not proof of causality. Normalized finger coordinates are not the absolute wire target.
response.denominator: All configured planned events remain in events + futureEvents. dueEvents and futureCensoredEvents are separate. Coalesced, blocked, clipped, unchanged and unsubmitted events cannot be inferred successful. Hold markers do not manufacture a wire edge.

scopes.timing: callbackCompletionGapMs is the post-native sampledAt gap between renderer submissions, not whole observer callback return; RAF timestamps and submissions are not physical scanout.
scopes.phase: scenes is a compatibility alias of sessionPhases (SessionPhase, not internal MatchScene); no phase is excluded.
scopes.capture: captures is a once-only input-capture counter and may be ahead of simulation completion; it never chooses boundaries.
scopes.nativeWork: callbackWorkMs is the existing native game callback measurement, not total JavaScript observer time or GPU completion.

wireObservation.boundary: Serialized native local input first observed at the transport send-intent hook, before original send and configured client delay/drop.
wireObservation.timing: firstWireAtMs is this observation time. It is not successful send API completion, network delivery, or the exact native capture time.

source.clockIndependence: setTimeout absolute deadlines; never scheduled from game frame, capture, frontier or transport progress.

tape.scope: Rechecks retained unique 12B rows; duplicate packet comparisons remain probe-reported.

response.method: Conditional render-progress proxy: latest submitted movement event, first subsequent changed native movement wire, then first newly advanced frontier with renderer submission. This does not establish visible movement or per-event gameplay effect.
response.confounding: Focus can change joystick velocity; death/context changes can write neutral input; clipping, overwritten moves and target convergence can produce no visible movement. First wire observation can follow a capture delayed by backpressure: ordering it after an event does not prove capture followed that event. The submission touch state and changed-controls marker are metadata, not proof of causality. Normalized finger coordinates are not the absolute wire target.
response.denominator: All configured planned events remain in events + futureEvents. dueEvents and futureCensoredEvents are separate. Coalesced, blocked, clipped, unchanged and unsubmitted events cannot be inferred successful. Hold markers do not manufacture a wire edge.

rafAnomaly.scope: Poll observations of an existing game RAF chain. No new frames, timers, transport processing, trace capture, or production fallback. The 250 ms trigger is diagnostic, not a smoothness acceptance threshold.

clocks.pollGaps: Gaps between observations are not proof that RAF or JavaScript was blocked; only an identified request supplies wait evidence.

A pending request observed after pause/stop remains in finalObservation; its active interval is censored, not automatically a game freeze.
Pre/post history is at most 32 actual polls each, not a guaranteed duration; omitted polls and final pending are retained explicitly.

rafAnomalyNodePolls.scope: Existing 100 ms status-poll CDP request/return brackets. Page clocks are separate; a missing poll is not proof of a pending RAF.

host.scope: Host-wide counters, not per-call CPU attribution. Process deltas require adjacent same pid/name.
limitations: Aggregate CPU occupancy does not establish single-core availability, CPU frequency, thermal state, GPU load, or a stable benchmark environment.
Process names are candidates for contention, not proof that a process is compiling. Known harness/relay/helper PIDs are labeled separately; other node processes remain unlabeled candidates.
Process CPU is cumulative lifetime CPU seconds. A first sighting is not CPU consumed during this run; PID reuse or counter reset can break a delta.
The 5 s process snapshots miss short tasks that start and exit between snapshots. Timer delays and source/receive times are retained.
This observer has overhead. Its own PowerShell helper is intentionally not a candidate process, but its work is included in aggregate CPU counters.
Overflow and sampling failures make this evidence incomplete; they are never a reason to silently remove a game result.

methods.body: Frozen first-cross native-frontier [s,e). Every body callback cost retained; counters/Hz close e-s. Endpoint cost is tail.
methods.work: sample[2] is whole C++ rAF callback elapsed, potentially zero/multiple ticks, synchronous send/audio/draw included. Not pure Tick/Restore CPU.
methods.fresh: Adjacent next/capture/renderer deltas exactly 1, correction/resim deltas 0, next equals native frontier. Still whole callback elapsed.
methods.repairs: stats[5] and sample[8] count RepairsSent. repairsDelta closes e-s. Return code 2 includes waiting/recovery; it does not prove network waiting.
methods.clocks: sampledAt is post-native observation; RAF timestamps remain distinct, neither is physical scanout. Cross-process joins require compatible observed clock brackets covering the context; otherwise only input-frame association is retained.
methods.touch: All planned/due/future/coalesced/unsubmitted denominators retained. Conditional wire-to-render progress does not prove movement or physical input response.
methods.failure: Missing reports use their failure artifact if present. Earlier preflight failure remains separately with source record, invocation/log SHA and first failure text.
